flags.title: OLBG lists no snooker markets at all
flags.detail: The snooker hub returns 'No tips found.' and its own sport filter renders as 'All Sports' rather than 'Snooker'. There is no event, no market and no tip count to price, so the board carries zero snooker picks and zero snooker lines. Nothing was substituted from another source.

flags.title: Greyhounds page empty today, eight races yesterday
flags.detail: The same URL that carried eight races on the 26 October capture returns 'No tips found.' today. Racecards for this evening's UK meetings had not been posted by OLBG at 05:30 UTC. No runner, trap or price is invented to fill the page.

flags.title: OLBG shows 'Tie' as the most popular handball pick on 13 of 15 events
flags.detail: Every EHF Champions League row on the hub prints 'Tie' as the most-tipped selection, with shares between 43 and 78 per cent. A draw is never the most-backed outcome in a handball match at that rate, so the field is treated as a display fault. The draw price is excluded from every handball line and the side prices are built from the EHF group table instead.

flags.title: OLBG kick-off times disagree with EHF by five hours
flags.detail: OLBG prints 13:45 and 15:45 for the 28 October Champions League round; the EHF's own calendar prints 18:45 and 20:45 CET for the same fixtures. The five-hour gap is consistent across all seven matches, so it looks like a timezone setting rather than a typo, but we cannot tell which clock OLBG is using. Our pages quote OLBG's label and the EHF time side by side.

flags.title: No match-level rugby league markets, only three season ante-posts
flags.detail: The hub lists State of Origin 2027, Super League 2027 and NRL 2027, all outrights settling in 2027. There is no fixture to price for this week, so rugby league gets three low-confidence ante-post picks rather than five match picks.

flags.title: One published pick sits shorter than the -250 floor
flags.detail: Eire Og Cor +0.50 at Kanturk is priced at -326 by this board, outside the -250 to +10000 band the brief asks us to work in. It is kept on the site because the 6-of-6 tip split is the most one-sided market on the card, and it is labelled 'outside band' wherever it appears.

flags.title: Golf carries three tournaments, one tipped selection each, two tips per market
flags.detail: Maybank Championship, Mexico Open and Simmons Bank Championship each show a single selection on 1 of 2 win tips. The Mexico Open event page lists a full field but every other player is on 0 of 2. Three low-confidence each-way picks is the honest maximum; a five-pick golf card would be padding.

flags.title: Seven sports have no official form source in this build
flags.detail: Volleyball, rugby union, golf, darts, motor racing, rugby league and the domestic cricket fixtures are priced from the OLBG tip split alone. No official league table, team sheet or injury report was read for them, so no form, standings or injury claim appears in those predictions. Each such card says so in its own 'not checked' line.

flags.title: The three strongest cricket lines are on matches already under way
flags.detail: New Zealand v India 3rd T20 (03:00), Pakistan v Sri Lanka (04:00) and Namibia v Ireland (03:30) were all in progress when the capture was taken at 05:30 UTC. Their lines price at -239, -222 and -204, which would have been the three highest-confidence in-band cricket picks, but a pick on a live match is not a pre-match prediction, so they are excluded and only the upcoming fixtures are published.

flags.title: OLBG prints no competition for tennis, and only the Basel pairings could be checked
flags.detail: The tennis hub gives player names and a start time with no tournament label. Five of the published picks were matched to the ATP's own Basel draw report; the Paul v Rublev card could not be tied to a tournament and says so.

flags.title: Four totals markets have no tips at all and are priced at a 50/50 prior
flags.detail: Panathinaikos v Milano Over/Under 164.50 and Milwaukee @ Tampa Bay Over/Under 7.50 each show 0 of 0 win tips. Our line for them is the uninformative prior at -104 both ways. They are published so that every listed market has a price, they are labelled 'unrated', and the only one used as a pick is the baseball under, which is explicitly low confidence.

flags.title: Two rows were cut off mid-page and are left unpriced
flags.detail: The Sultanbeyli Bld v Gebze Genclik volleyball row and the Virtus Bologna v Zalgiris basketball row both lost their tip split when the page was cut. Both are left with null fields in the capture file rather than a guess.

flags.title: OLBG prints no market name for the two club football rows
flags.detail: Kanturk v Eire Og Cor and Fr Caseys v Kildimo Pallaskenry both appear with a blank market field and a points line (+0.50 and +3.50). The lines look like a points handicap, so that is how we label them, but the label is ours and not OLBG's.

flags.title: Eight of the fifteen sports cannot reach five picks today
flags.detail: Snooker 0, greyhounds 0, darts 2, motor racing 2, golf 3, gaelic 3, rugby league 3, baseball 3. In each case the reason is the number of markets OLBG published, not a shortage of effort: the hub was read in full. Padding these sports to five would have meant pricing selections that OLBG does not list.

flags.title: NHL table is dated 26 October, one day before the board
flags.detail: The standings snapshot used for the two NHL picks is dated 26 October on NHL.com. Games played on the evening of 26 October may not be reflected. The page is cited with its date on every card that uses it.

flags.title: No starting pitchers were announced for World Series Game 4
flags.detail: MLB.com listed the Game 4 time and venue but no probables, so the pitching matchup is not part of any baseball pick. In a market where pitching drives the price, that is a material blank.

blanks.why: No injury feed was reachable for any of the fifteen sports at capture time.
